messages:
anya: Heads-up — running into fragmented JSON objects over SSE in our Java client. Using OkHttp EventSource; large responses get chunked mid-object and our parser chokes. Anyone handled this cleanly?
michael: Yup. Two options: 1) switch server to NDJSON or explicit delimiters (easiest). 2) use a non-blocking streaming parser on the client (jackson async) and feed bytes as they arrive.
raj: FWIW we saw similar with Node where newline delimiting saved us. But Java libs matter. cc @michael do we have a short example for jackson async?
michael: Quick sketch — non-blocking parser pattern:
```java
JsonFactory jf = new JsonFactory();
JsonParser p = jf.createNonBlockingByteArrayParser(); // jackson core
((NonBlockingJsonParser)p).feedInput(buf, 0, len);
JsonToken t;
while ((t = p.nextToken()) != null) {
  // handle tokens; complete objects arrive in stream
}
```
Caveats: need to use jackson-core 2.9+ and cast to non-blocking impl. Strings containing braces can still confuse naive brace-count hacks.
olivia: If you can't pull jackson async into the client, a pragmatic fallback is to accumulate bytes until a top-level object completes (brace counter), but escape-aware parsing is required. Also consider asking the backend to emit an explicit "event: done" or a delimiter between objects in SSE `data:` blocks.
anya: Is there a way to signal backpressure to OkHttp/EventSource so we don't read so fast? The problem is client keeps buffering lots of partials.
michael: OkHttp doesn't expose a nice pause API on EventSource. Options:
- Use a lower-level WebClient where you control read buffer sizes and pause reads.
- Use an executor to process and apply backpressure: stop consuming application-level queue while letting TCP window handle back-pressure (not ideal).
- If using Jetty/Netty on server side, add smaller chunking or throttle server send.
olivia: Another angle: add small ACK events from client to server (custom SSE event) so server pauses until ack; requires server changes but simplest semantically.
anya: Thanks. For immediate unblock I can try jackson async. michael — can you drop a tiny example into PR #1234? I'm close to shipping the java client fix.
michael: Yep I'll add a small unit test and example. Quick note: when testing, simulate fragments that split inside strings, escaped quotes, unicode to validate parser.
raj: created issue INF-789 to track server-side delimiter work and cross-language compatibility.
devex-bot: Automated note: created ticket INF-789 and linked PR #1234 for follow-up tasks :white_check_mark:
anya: One more quick Q — auth retries: if stream disconnects mid-object, should client attempt to resume or restart? I think restart and re-request full object unless server supports resume.
michael: Agree — restart. Implement idempotent request semantics or server-provided resume tokens. For now we should retry with exponential backoff and clear partial buffers.
anya: Awesome, thanks all. I'll try jackson async and ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:
